title: Shared Morphs, Infinite Canvas, Optical Trim, Cursor Glow & Radial Menu
description: Five live drops: a same-document view-transition morph, a pan-forever chunked canvas, the new text-box-trim optical type, a cursor spotlight glow, and a radial context menu.

drops.title: Shared-Element Morph
drops.description: Click a thumbnail and watch it fluidly morph into the full detail view via the same-document View Transitions API.
drops.concept: Both the thumbnail and its detail-view target get a matching view-transition-name set right before document.startViewTransition() runs the DOM swap. The browser snapshots old and new states per name and auto-generates ::view-transition-group/-old/-new pseudo-elements that it cross-fades and geometrically interpolates between — no manual FLIP math required. A debug panel exposes the shared duration and easing as CSS custom properties consumed by those pseudo-elements.
drops.source: MDN View Transition API docs + Animation Patterns' shared-element layout transition demo

interaction.mouse: Click any card to open its morphed detail view
interaction.click: Click 'Back to grid' to reverse the morph

drops.title: Infinite Chunked Canvas
drops.description: A spatial canvas you can drag/pan forever in any direction — content streams in and out with zero loading stutter.
drops.concept: Space is divided into fixed-size chunks; only chunks within a buffer radius of the current camera offset exist in the DOM at once. Each chunk's color, shape and rotation are derived from a deterministic integer hash of its (col,row) coordinates, so panning back to the same spot always regenerates identical content — chunks can be destroyed and recreated with no visual discontinuity. Panning uses Pointer Events with simple velocity-based inertia after release.
drops.source: Codrops, 'Infinite Canvas: Building a Seamless, Pan-Anywhere Image Space' (Jan 2026), reimplemented in vanilla DOM/CSS instead of WebGL

interaction.mouse: Drag to pan; release for momentum
interaction.click: Recenter button jumps back to the origin
interaction.touch: Same drag-and-release gesture via Pointer Events

drops.title: Optical Text Trim
drops.description: The brand-new text-box-trim / text-box-edge CSS properties finally kill the phantom whitespace above and below headline type.
drops.concept: text-box-trim specifies which edge (trim-start, trim-end, trim-both) to shave off a text block's leading, while text-box-edge (e.g. cap alphabetic, text, ex) sets how much space to trim based on the font's own metrics. Toggling it live against a dashed-line frame shows large type snap flush against its box instead of floating in font-metric half-leading, with a measured pixel readout of the shrinking gap.
drops.source: MDN text-box-trim / text-box-edge docs + CSS WG 'Safe to Release' resolution (2026)

interaction.mouse: Toggle each example's trim switch to compare before/after
interaction.click: Change the edge-metric dropdown to retune all examples live

drops.title: Cursor Spotlight Glow
drops.description: A soft light literally follows your cursor across a dark card grid, illuminating each card's border and interior only where it touches.
drops.concept: A single document-level pointermove listener writes --x/--y CSS custom properties onto every card, rAF-throttled to one write per frame. A masked radial-gradient pseudo-element (mask-composite:exclude against a content-box mask) reveals the gradient only along the card's 1px border ring, while a second, dimmer radial-gradient behind the content adds an interior wash — both centered on the same live coordinates.

interaction.mouse: Move across any card to trace its border and interior glow
interaction.click: Radius and glow-color sliders retune every card live
interaction.touch: touchmove drives the same effect on mobile

drops.title: Radial Context Menu
drops.description: Right-click or long-press and a circular ring of actions blooms around your cursor instead of a boring vertical list.
drops.concept: Menu items are laid out as donut wedges via SVG arc paths, each spanning 360°/itemCount. Instead of hit-testing individual DOM rectangles, selection is direction-based: on move, Math.atan2(dy,dx) from the menu's origin to the pointer is mapped to a wedge index, which is highlighted live. Desktop uses contextmenu-to-open plus hover-then-click-to-confirm; touch uses a long-press timer to open, drag to select, and release to confirm — a marking-menu interaction pattern.

interaction.mouse: Right-click to open, move to highlight, click to confirm
interaction.click: Click outside or press Escape to cancel
interaction.touch: Long-press to open, drag to select, lift to confirm
